title: First Spritesheet... How do I set a grid perfectly around this? (Using this template).

posts.author: Bonyleg
posts.body: Just trying to get the grid to fit around the characters so that I don't have to move each individual character and center them myself. Very new to all of this. Any help would be appreciated. I'm using Gimp. Thanks.

posts.author: Puppet Knight
posts.body:
Go to Image -> Configure grid
To figure out what size each cell divide the width by 3 and the height by 4

posts.author: Apocalypticat
posts.body: Maybe not what you want to hear - but if you're going to put custom graphics in your game, there will be quite a lot of manual positioning and placement involved. So, best advice is to get used to manually placing/positioning them one by one and lining them up one by one. We personally use Paint.net instead of Gimp, since we know it better and we're more comfortable with it. Best of luck.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
as mentioned above the grid is a tool, it does not automate any correction needed to do the positioning.
and the ease of use you want to have is only possible if the source and the destination have the same cell size - as soon as different cell sizes are involved, you'll have to do manual positioning for a correct center.
the following tutorial might help you understand more:
How to create your own templates (any sprite or battler sheet) | RPG Maker Forums

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
For what it's worth my advice it to get a graphics editor that lets you overlay a grid on the screen, there are many. And make the grid the size of your character or tile-set etc. That way you can fit objects to te grid for a tile set and centre your character graphics.
It is the single most useful thing for fitting your graphics to size IMO
I quite like Aseprite or Pixel Studio, both of which are simple pixel drawing apps with a decent grid option.
